assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy link basic hormone biology (proglucagon processing, glucose-dependent insulin secretion, central appetite effects) to a transformative treatment class for type 2 diabetes and obesity with large cardiometabolic outcome benefits. Originality, clarity and societal impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Drucker and Holst established GLP-1 physiology and its biological actions; Mojsov's contribution on the active peptide form (GLP-1 7-36) is significant but the allocation among her, Habener-type early work and the drug developers (Knudsen) is debated, so a fair three-person configuration is plausible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, multiple approved drugs and large randomized outcome trials; recognition is timely and the interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between early peptide discovery, physiology and drug development (Knudsen) is unresolved
Whether the committee prefers the physiology or the therapeutic-development framing
My recall of the precise priority claims is from memory and not independently verified

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, cell-type-specific, millisecond control of activity and became a general tool across circuits, behavior and disease models; its impact on mapping circuits, including motor and spinal circuits, is broad and well documented.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and demonstration of neuronal use (Boyden, Deisseroth, Miesenböck) are both decisive; the three-person limit forces difficult exclusions and the field's priority disputes remain unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Over fifteen years of broad independent adoption and clinical translation beginning (retinal vision restoration); recognition is mature.
uncertainties: Three-person limit excludes Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck
Priority and credit disputes between discovery and neuronal-application contributions
Clinical therapeutic impact is still early

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defined how cytosolic DNA is sensed and converted into interferon and inflammatory responses, with implications for infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunity and aging; a clear conceptual advance with a defined molecular pathway.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cGAMP second messenger; Barber identified STING. Ishikawa shared STING discovery, and Sun and Wu contributed to cGAS work, so the credit is reasonably concentrated in two or three people but Ishikawa's role is a point of dispute.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is strongly confirmed; therapeutic agonists and antagonists are still in clinical trials, so translational validation is incomplete but fundamental recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Ishikawa's claim relative to Barber for STING
Therapeutic benefit not yet established
Related earlier work on DNA sensing and cyclic dinucleotides by others

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new organelle-to-nucleus signaling logic (IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing, ATF6, PERK), central to proteostasis, secretory physiology and diseases from diabetes to neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently and jointly defined the pathway and its signaling mechanism; this is a compact and widely accepted two-person configuration, though Ron and Harding are relevant to the PERK branch.
assessment.maturity: Mature, strongly confirmed foundational biology; direct clinical translation (such as ISRIB-type modulators) is still emerging.
uncertainties: Contributions of PERK-branch investigators may be argued
Medical impact is more indirect than for therapeutic candidates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR defined the central growth and nutrient-sensing kinase pathway linking nutrients and hormones to anabolism, with relevance to cancer, metabolism, immunosuppression and aging.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically and its role in growth control; Schreiber's work on rapamycin target binding (FKBP12-rapamycin) and mTOR identification was decisive. Sabatini contributed mTOR pathway biology, but I leave him out here given the allocation and sensitivities around that credit.
assessment.maturity: Very strongly confirmed and mature; rapalogs are in clinical use, though benefit in aging and cancer is still partial.
uncertainties: Competing claims for mammalian TOR identification (Sabatini, Sabers, Brown, Schreiber)
Exclusion of Sabatini is a judgment under the three-name limit
Rapamycin discovery itself predates this candidate

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splicing modulation by antisense oligonucleotide for SMN2 produced nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, which changed a fatal childhood motor neuron disease and established an RNA drug paradigm; it is also relevant to motor system disease.
assessment.attribution: Krainer's mechanistic splice-switching work and Bennett's oligonucleotide chemistry and development are decisive and form a natural pair; other contributors (such as Hua, Singh and academic groups in SMN biology, including Lefebvre and Melki for the gene) may argue for credit.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term clinical follow-up; the translational proof is strong, though the field is still evolving and the prize connection to earlier RNA recognitions is a factor.
uncertainties: Whether SMN1 gene discovery should be paired with the therapy
Other contributors to the oligonucleotide development
Overlap with prior RNA-related prizes

assessment.nobel_worthiness: CAR-T cell therapy created durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies by engineering T cells with synthetic receptors; a major clinical advance in oncology and cell therapy.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June contributed key CAR design (costimulation) and clinical translation; Rosenberg contributed adoptive cell therapy and early CAR trials. Eshhar's original chimeric receptor concept is not among the credited names, which weakens the fairness of the configuration.
assessment.maturity: Approved products with long follow-up, though toxicity, solid tumor limits and durability issues remain; recognition is plausible but possibly premature relative to maturity of the field.
uncertainties: Eshhar and other early inventors are not credited
Long-term safety and solid-tumor efficacy are unresolved
Rosenberg's inclusion is arguable because his work is adoptive therapy more broadly

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult stem-cell-derived organoids (from Lgr5 stem cells) created self-organizing, expandable three-dimensional tissue models transforming study of tissue renewal, infection, cancer and disease modeling.
assessment.attribution: Clevers identified Lgr5 stem cells and led the organoid culture breakthrough with sato as first author, so a two-person configuration is defensible, although parallel work on pluripotent-stem-cell-derived organoids (Sasai and others) and Wnt/niche concepts overlap.
assessment.maturity: Rapid and wide adoption with independent confirmation, though therapeutic impact and standardization are still developing, so the timing may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Overlap with pluripotent-stem-cell organoid work not credited here
Medical impact is still mostly experimental
Sato's inclusion as a trainee versus a senior leader is a judgment call
